summary: A toggle for an on/off setting, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the track and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from reaching the inner input.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: Current state (on). Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Must be on to submit (valueMissing). Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled: dimmed, cannot toggle, not submitted. Also set by a disabled ancestor fieldset.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: track in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Track wrapper; positions the thumb over the native input.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">; receives focus, Space and validation. Fills the track, visually transparent.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Circle that slides from the start to the end of the track (mirrored in RTL). Decorative, aria-hidden.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring in ring color (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: On: track in primary, thumb at the end. Off is the base look: track in the input border color (3:1), thumb at the start; state is shown by thumb position as well as color (WCAG 1.4.1).

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals: setFormValue(value) only while on, validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing), formResetCallback restores the default checked state from the checked attribute, formDisabledCallback applies a disabled fieldset, disabled is not submitted.

accessibility.targetSize: The track is 32x20px (24x16px in sm), under 24px high; the label is part of the clickable row and the 12px gap satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color around the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009). Enter does not toggle.

aria: role="switch" on the native input; checked state exposed as aria-checked
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)
the new state (on/off) is announced by the switch role on toggle; no extra live text

useCases.when: A setting that is on or off
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label that names the setting

useCases.when: The setting needs a consequence explained
A setting must be on before submit
useCases.use: required with a label that states it

antiPatterns.pattern: A yes/no choice recorded only on submit, or one of several options
antiPatterns.why: Checkboxes record a choice; a switch implies the setting is on or off

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing exactly one option from several
antiPatterns.why: A switch has two states for one setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state, such as Enable / Disable
antiPatterns.why: The switch role announces the state; a changing label reads twice or contradicts it
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting

antiPatterns.pattern: An action rather than a setting

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: APG switch pattern, label row beside the track. Mirrors the Checkbox contract where behavior is shared.

openQuestions.question: Native input type=checkbox with role=switch, or a custom element with role=switch?
openQuestions.answer: Native input with role=switch: native Space, focus, required validity and form value, as SB-0007 asks (native elements first).

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No. Same as Checkbox: the attribute is the default that form reset restores; checked is a property.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, like Checkbox and Input. hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: What does required mean for a switch?
openQuestions.answer: It must be on to submit (native valueMissing), like a required checkbox; for must-accept settings only.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle or submit?
openQuestions.answer: Enter submits the form via form.requestSubmit() (SB-0009) and does not toggle; only Space toggles. APG leaves Enter optional for switch.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes?
openQuestions.answer: default (32x20px track) and sm (24x16px), using the existing size.switch tokens.

openQuestions.question: How is the off state kept at 3:1 and not color-only?
openQuestions.answer: Off track uses color.input (3:1 against the background, WCAG 1.4.11) and thumb position also shows state (1.4.1). Deviation from a translucent off track in the visual reference.

openQuestions.question: Is there a loading or indeterminate state?
openQuestions.answer: No. A switch is strictly on or off.
